COMMIT: OK I read the diff, the new test file and the `studio-repeat-safe` helper. I did not run a browser; the points about event ordering and focus are from reading the code. **Scope.** The candidate commit touches only `app/routes/account.tsx`, the new test `app/lib/__tests__/account-profile-name.test.tsx` and the implementation doc. Nothing in auth, purchase or download code changes. `updateProfile` and `updatePassword` are still called exactly as before, and there is no new `any`, assertion or suppression directive. **Findings, ranked (none blocking):** 1. **Low – `app/routes/account.tsx:276`, `active:transform-none!`.** - A global rule in `app/styles/app.css:230` (`button:active…`) applies a press transform to every button. - The override is a Tailwind v4 important modifier, and `account.orders.tsx:69` already uses the same pattern, so it is consistent. - It does leave the name button without any press feedback. Only fix this if that matters to you; if so, drop the override and accept the global press effect. 2. **Low – `app/routes/account.tsx:10`, import from `~/components/arrangement/studio-repeat-safe`.** - The account route now depends on a helper that lives in the arrangement (Studio) folder. - The helper is a pure 5-line function with no Studio state, so behavior is fine. The cost is the coupling direction. - Fix: when convenient, move it to a neutral place such as `~/lib`, or `~/components/ui`. Don't do this in this commit. 3. **Low – `app/routes/account.tsx:262-264`, Save and Cancel buttons.** - These two icon buttons still have no `focus-visible` ring classes and no `disabled:` styling. Disabled state is conveyed only by the `disabled` attribute. - This predates the diff. The visible-focus check belongs in the real-browser pass, since the global focus style may already cover it. 4. **Info – `app/routes/account.tsx:96,132-137`, the `restoreNameFocusRef` / `isNameEditorFocusUnclaimed` logic.** - **Safari and iOS:** buttons don't take focus on click there, so `activeElement` is `body` after clicking Save. That case is handled as "unclaimed", so focus returns to the name button, and the tests PN10c and PN10d cover it. - **Disabled Save button:** after the click, Save is disabled while the save is in flight. In Chrome the disabled button can stay as `activeElement`, and `contains` still counts it as inside the editor, so that case is covered too. - **Unmount during a save:** `setIsEditingName` and `setNameSaving` run after unmount, but they are harmless no-ops in React 18. There are no timers or listeners to leak, because the diff adds only refs and one effect that has a deps array. - **Stale focus-restore flag:** if the effect doesn't run (the editor is already closed), `restoreNameFocusRef` stays true. The next `isEditingName` false-to-true change takes the focus-input branch first. It only restores after the editor closes again, and that is the intended behavior. 5. **Info – render cost.** There are no new state updates and no per-render allocations beyond two small closures. `useId` is stable. Cost is negligible. 6. **Info – accessibility is improved.** - The `
